study_type: simulation study with reinforcement learning agents
setting: Enhanced Reconfigurable Manufacturing System (EnhancedRMS) environment, a flexible job shop with 5 machines, 50 jobs, dynamic setup operations and stochastic machine breakdowns
sample_or_dataset: 50 jobs per episode, 1000 episodes per configuration; 5 independent runs per workload; 5 scheduling strategies compared
ai_method: Dueling-Attention Deep Q-Network (EnhancedDQN) with negotiation-driven coordination (deep reinforcement learning with multi‑agent negotiation)
comparison: PPO, SAC, EDF heuristic, Random baseline, and configurations with/without reconfiguration and negotiation (WNR, WTR, WNF, WTF)
key_findings: The negotiation‑driven EnhancedDQN achieved the lowest makespan (average 177.3 time units across configurations) and lowest total tardiness (average 312.7 time units) compared to other strategies. It also maintained high machine utilization (average 21.1%) while incurring moderate reconfiguration overhead (average 108.2 time units). In breakdown scenarios, the combined approach reduced makespan by 15.5% relative to reconfiguration‑only and improved utilization by 9.3 percentage points, achieving 100% job completion.
limitations: Results are based on a custom simulation environment; real‑world validation is lacking. The study reports variability due to stochastic disruptions but does not explore scalability to larger systems or multiple resource types. Computational efficiency and integration with existing manufacturing execution systems were not evaluated.
title: A Negotiation-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach for Dynamic Scheduling of Reconfigurable Manufacturing Systems

exclusion_reason: No data on dynamic production planning and scheduling under disruptions is reported in the provided passage.
title: Deep reinforcement learning based preventive maintenance policy for serial production lines

setting: semiconductor manufacturing capacity planning using discrete-event simulation
sample_or_dataset: Intel’s small-scale Minifab (5 machines, 3 products) and SMT2020 testbed (1,314 machines, 583 processing steps, LV/HM dataset)
ai_method: deep reinforcement learning with a heterogeneous graph neural network (HGNN) trained via PPO
comparison: heuristic baseline, random actions, and no-action baseline
key_findings: In the Minifab environment, the HGNN policy increased completed lots by 1.59% and reduced cycle time by 2.70% versus the heuristic, and by 13.85%/14.96% versus no action. In the larger SMT2020 testbed, the policy improved completed lots by 1.87% (≈110 lots) and reduced cycle time by 1.80% (≈1.08 days) versus the heuristic, and by 2.50%/2.33% versus no action, yielding an overall throughput increase of about 1.8%.
limitations: Results are based on simulation testbeds; real‑world deployment and cost considerations were not evaluated; training stability over long horizons remains to be addressed.
title: Learning to Optimize Capacity Planning in Semiconductor Manufacturing

study_type: simulation study using high‑fidelity digital twin
sample_or_dataset: high‑fidelity simulator based on real industrial data; 30 scenario–seed evaluation instances from 10 test scenarios and 3 seeds each
ai_method: deep reinforcement learning with event‑driven temporal‑difference formulation; algorithms evaluated include DQL, SAC, PPO, CQL, IQL
comparison: random policy, shortest processing time (SPT) heuristic, first‑in‑first‑out (FIFO) baseline
key_findings: Agents trained offline and online achieved significant and consistent gains in throughput and utilization compared to random, SPT, and FIFO baselines. Offline training with conservative algorithms (CQL, IQL) produced performance close to DQL, while online off‑policy methods (DQL, SAC) were more sample‑efficient and on‑policy PPO was more sensitive to data. Overall, the event‑driven RL framework enabled scalable, generalizable control in a large‑scale, stochastic semiconductor fab.
limitations: State and action representations were feature‑based; learned encoders, graph‑based or foundation‑model representations were not explored. Hyperparameter tuning and benchmarking across algorithms were limited; model‑based agents and self‑supervised dynamics learning were suggested for future work.
title: Event-Driven Reinforcement Learning Enables Long-Horizon Control in Semiconductor Fabrication
